name: GO Classes Test Series 2023 | NIELIT Mock Test 2

question.text:
A train, moving at a speed of $45 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$, passes a man running at a speed of $9 \;\mathrm{km} / \mathrm{hr}$ in the same direction as that of train, in $20$ seconds. Find the length of train in meters.

  1. $100$
  2. $200$
  3. $300$
  4. $400$

He has great antipathy _______ those who are hypocrites.
  1. for
  2. to
  3. against
  4. from

Find the missing number.

$27: 51:: 83:$______

  1. $102$
  2. $117$
  3. $123$
  4. $138$

Find out the part of the sentence which is grammatically incorrect

He was(A)  so ashamed(B)  and he left(C)  the place(D).

For integers $a, b$ and $c$, what would be the minimum and maximum values respectively of $a+b+c$ if $\log |a|+\log |b|+\log |c|=0 ?$

  1. $-3$ and $3$
  2. $-1$ and $1$
  3. $-1$ and $3$
  4. $1$ and $3$

A cube of side $1$ meter length is cut into small cubes of side $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ each. How many such cubes can be formed?

  1. $10$
  2. $100$
  3. $1000$
  4. $10000$

A sum of money doubles in $12$ years. In how many years will it treble?

  1. $12$
  2. $6$
  3. $24$
  4. $8$

A window is made up of a square portion and an equilateral triangle portion above it. The base of the triangular portion coincides with the upper side of the square. If the perimeter of the window is $6 \mathrm{~m}$, the area of the window is _______ $\mathrm{m}^2$.

  1. $1.43$
  2. $2.06$
  3. $2.68$
  4. $2.88$

If the $1$st January of any particular year is Monday, what is the day on $1$st June of the same year? Consider the year is a non-leap year.

  1. Monday
  2. Tuesday
  3. Saturday
  4. Friday

Dishonesty is always detrimental progress in life.
  1. to
  2. for
  3. in
  4. None

If the time in wall clock is $4: 20$, what will be the time in the mirror image of the clock?
  1. $8: 40$
  2. $8: 20$
  3. $7:40$
  4. $7: 20$

Maya her driving test unless she calms down.
  1. Doesn't pass
  2. Didn't pass
  3. Will not pass
  4. Wouldn't be passing

Through an inlet, a tank takes $8$ hours to get filled up. Due to a leak in the bottom, it takes $2$ hours more to get it filled completely. If the tank is full, how much time will the leak take to empty it?

  1. $16$ hours
  2. $20$ hours
  3. $32$ hours
  4. $40$ hours

$1$ quality of wheat at Rs. $9.3$ per kg mixed with another quality at a certain rate in the ratio of $8:7.$ If the mixture so formed is worth $\mathrm{Rs} .10 \mathrm{per} \mathrm{kg}$, what is the rate per $\mathrm{kg}$ of the second quality of wheat?

  1. Rs. $10.30$
  2. Rs $10.60$

What is the sum of all the even numbers from $11$ to $381 ?$

  2. $32620$
  3. $36260$

India got freedom on $15$th August $1947.$ What day was it?

  1. Friday
  2. Sunday
  3. Thursday       
  4. Monday

If the speed of boat in still water is $5 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$ and the speed of stream is $2 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}$, how much time will it take for boat to cover $70 \mathrm{~km}$ downstream?

  1. $15$ hours
  2. $20$ hours
  3. $5$ hours
  4. $10$ hours

If $a<b, d>c$ and $a<d,$ which of the following is true?

  1. $b<c$
  2. $c>a$
  1. Only $1$
  2. Neither $1$ nor $2$
  3. Only $2$
  4. Both $1$ and $2$

Starting from his house, Sachin walks a distance of $8 \mathrm{~m}$ towards north, then he turns left and walks $6 \mathrm{~m}$, then walks $3 \mathrm{~m}$ towards south and finally travels $6 \mathrm{~m}$ towards the west. to reach his office. What is the distance between his house and office and also find in which direction is his office situated with respect to his house.

  1. $7$ meters, South-East
  2. $7$ meters, South-West
  3. $13$ meters, North-West
  4. $17$ meters, South-West

In how many years will a sum of $1875$ amount to $2187$ at $8 \%$ p.a. compound interest?

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $4$

A father said to his son, "I was as old as you are at present at the time of your birth. If the father's age is $38$ now, the son's age $5$ years back is:

  1. $14$
  2. $19$
  3. $33$
  4. $38$

A man gets back the amount he had invested in buying $100$ radios by selling $65$ of them. What is his profit percentage?

Statement 1: Some villages are poor
Statement 2: All poor are nice people

Conclusion 1: Some nice people are villagers
Conclusion 2: No villagers are nice people

  4. Neither $1$ nor $2$ follows

Mohan began a business with Rs. $45000.$ He was joined afterwards by Sohan with Rs. $54000.$ If at the end of the year, the profit was shared in the ratio of $2: 1,$ after how many months did Sohan join the business?

  1. $4$
  2. $5$

  1. Rajesh and Hitesh

Find the remainder of $3^{43}$ when divided by $4.$

  2. $1$

$\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ can complete a piece of work in $9$ and $12$ days, respectively. If they work on alternate days starting from $\text{A},$ in how many days will the work be completed?

  1. $10$

An FM signal with modulation index $m_f$ is passed through a frequency tripler. The modulation index of the output signal will be
  1. $m_f$

  4. $27 m_f$

A fitness test is done on our Indian Cricket team players. Assume $4 \%$ of our cricket players are unfit and our test result shows positive results (i.e. a player being fit) on fit players $97 \%$ of the time and on unfit players $2 \%$ of the time.
What is the probability that a randomly chosen player with a positive result is actually fit?

  1. $0.57$
  2. $0.67$
  3. $0.77$
  4. $0.87$

Which one of the following is a closed form expression for the generating function of the sequence $\{a_n\}$ where $a_n = \binom {n+4}{n}$ for $n= 0,1,2,\ldots ?$

  2. $\dfrac{5}{(1-x)}$

     

  3. $\dfrac{1}{(1-x)^4}$

{

Consider a stack in which the numbers are pushed in the following order $2,3,4,6,5,1$, 0. What will be at the top of the stack after the following operations $\textsf{push(9), pop, pop, pop}$ respectively?

  1. $5$
  2. $1$

Every time an address line is added to a DRAM, the number of addressable locations in that DRAM is multiplied by a factor of

  1. $1.5$
  2. $2$
  3. $4$

What will be the result of the following code snippet?

  1. $45$

A box contains $10$ marbles: $3$ red, $4$ blue, and $3$ green. If two marbles are drawn at random without replacement, what is the probability that the first marble is red and the second marble is blue?

  1. $3 / 20$
  2. $2 / 15$
  3. $3 / 35$
  4. $3 / 42$

  1. $19 / 45$
  2. $8 / 45$

  4. $4 / 45$

void fun1(struct node* head) 
{

}

Suppose you are given an implementation of a queue of integers. The operations that can be performed on the queue are:

  1. $isEmpty (Q)$ — returns true if the queue is empty, false otherwise.
  2. $delete (Q)$ — deletes the element at the front of the queue and returns its value.
  3. $insert (Q, i)$ — inserts the integer $i$ at the rear of the queue.

Consider the following function:

void f (queue Q) {
int i ;
if (!isEmpty(Q)) {
   i = delete(Q);
   f(Q);
   insert(Q, i);
  }
}

What operation is performed by the above function $f?$ 

  1. Leaves the queue $Q$ unchanged
  2. Reverses the order of the elements in the queue $Q$
  3. Deletes the element at the front of the queue $Q$ and inserts it at the rear keeping the other elements in the same order
  4. Empties the queue $Q$

A small deck of five cards are numbered $1$ to $5.$ First one card and then a second card are selected at random, with replacement. What is the probability that the sum of the values on the cards is a prime number?

  1. $10 / 25$
  2. $11 / 25$
  3. $12 / 25$
  4. $13 / 25$

The bandwidth of a PCM system having two quantization levels is $\text{B}$. if the quantization level is increased to $8,$ the resultant bandwidth will be

  1. $\mathrm{B}$
  2. $2 \mathrm{~B}$
  3. $3 \mathrm{~B}$
  4. $4 \mathrm{~B}$

Consider the following table named $\text{“Employees":}$
$$
\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \textbf{emp_id} & \textbf{emp_name} & \textbf{department} & \textbf{salary} \\
\hline 1001 & \text{John Doe} & \text{HR} & 50000 \\
\hline 1002 & \text{Jane Smith} & \text{Sales} & 60000 \\
\hline 1003 & \text{Mike Brown} & \text{IT} & 55000 \\
\hline 1004 & \text{Emily Lee} & \text{HR} & 52000 \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$
Write an SQL query to retrieve the names of all employees in the Sales department.

Answer choices:

  1. SELECT emp_name FROM Employees WHERE department = 'Sales'
  2. SELECT department FROM Employees WHERE emp_name = 'Sales'
  3. SELECT emp_name FROM Employees WHERE department = 'Sales' AND emp_name = 'Sales'
  4. SELECT emp_name FROM Employees WHERE emp_name = 'Sales'

What is the worst-case number of comparisons in insertion sort?

  1. $f_m$

  3. $3 f_m$

What is the minimum number of tables required to represent this situation in the relational model?

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. $5$

Consider the following $\text{C}$ code segment:

a = b + c;
e = a + 1;
d = b + c;
f = d + 1;
g = e + f;

In a compiler, this code segment is represented internally as a directed acyclic graph $\text{(DAG)}$. The number of nodes in the $\text{DAG}$ is _____________

  1. superimposing a low frequency on a high frequency

    for(int j=0; j<N; j++)
    for(int k=N-2; k<N+2; k++)
    cout << i << " " << j << endl;

  2. $O(N \log N)$

$$
\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
